record.context_brief: Maximum flip distance between triangulations of an n-gon.
record.original_question: Let f(n) be the maximum graph distance between two triangulations of a fixed n-gon, where two triangulations are adjacent when one is obtained from the other by flipping a single diagonal inside a quadrilateral. Is the upper bound f(n) <= 2n - 10, valid for n >= 8, asymptotically and exactly optimal?

evidence.quote: It is easy to show f(n) < 2n - 10 (for n > 8), which is conjectured optimal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a fixed convex polygon with $n \ge 8$ vertices. A triangulation of $P$ is a maximal set of pairwise non-crossing diagonals of $P$, which subdivides $P$ into triangles. Two triangulations $T$ and $T'$ are said to be adjacent if there exist a diagonal $d \in T$ and a diagonal $d' \in T'$ such that $T' = (T \setminus \{d\}) \cup \{d'\}$; equivalently, $d$ and $d'$ are the two diagonals of some convex quadrilateral formed by two adjacent triangles of $T$, and replacing $d$ by $d'$ is called a diagonal flip. This adjacency relation defines the flip graph $\mathcal{F}_n$, whose vertices are the triangulations of $P$. Let $f(n)$ denote the diameter of $\mathcal{F}_n$, that is, the maximum, over all pairs of triangulations $T, T'$ of $P$, of the minimum number of flips needed to transform $T$ into $T'$.

It is known that $f(n) \le 2n - 10$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Determine whether this upper bound is tight: is it true that $f(n) = 2n - 10$ for all sufficiently large $n$ (and, more strongly, asymptotically optimal in the sense $f(n)/n \to 2$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture was settled by Lionel Pournin (2014), who gave a combinatorial proof that the diameter of the associahedron — equivalently, the maximum flip distance between two triangulations of a convex $n$-gon — equals $2n-10$ for all $n \ge 13$. This resolves the question posed originally by Sleator, Tarjan, and Thurston, who established the upper bound and proved tightness only for sufficiently large $n$ via hyperbolic geometry without an explicit threshold.

status_evidence.title: The diameter of associahedra (Pournin, Adv. Math. 2014)
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that the diameter of the n-dimensional associahedron is 2n-4 when n>9, settling a conjecture of Sleator, Tarjan and Thurston.
status_evidence.claim: Pournin proved the maximum flip distance equals 2n-10 for n>=13, confirming the conjectured optimal bound.

status_evidence.title: Flip distance - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The diameter of the flip graph of a convex n-gon is equal to 2n − 10 when n ≥ 13.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the exact value f(n)=2n-10 for n>=13.
